comparison.objective: Insert a cotter pin through a clevis pin and permanently bend both legs to secure the joint; candidate adjusts and reversibly locks a hydraulic damper setting.
comparison.physical_skill: Cotter task tests small-part pickup, hole alignment/insertion, and opposed plastic bending. Candidate tests recessed tool insertion, captive setscrew operation, controlled collar rotation, counterholding, and iterative response-based tuning.
comparison.success_condition: Full cotter success requires seating within stated positional/angular tolerances, both legs bent at least 45°, release, stability for 1 s, and no prohibited rebending. Candidate instead requires two acceptable energy-absorption cycles and post-lock setting retention; its thread-damage, torque, rebound, and drift numeric limits are missing.
comparison.reason: Generic small-part alignment is shared, but permanent fastener deformation after insertion is meaningfully different from reversible rotary adjustment and measured dynamic damping validation.
